title: Ankita Bhandari's Parents Detained at India Gate Over Governor Appointment Protest
excerpt: Virendra Singh Bhandari and Soni Devi were detained at about 4 am on 15 October and released within two hours, as they demanded Dushyant Kumar Gautam's appointment as Sikkim Governor be held pending the VIP-angle investigation — allegations Gautam denies.
body:
• Delhi Police detained Ankita Bhandari's parents at about 4 am on 15 October during an overnight sit-in at India Gate; they were released within about two hours.
  • The family is demanding that Dushyant Kumar Gautam's appointment as Governor of Sikkim be put on hold until the investigation into the alleged 'VIP' angle in the 2022 murder is complete.
  • Gautam has denied the allegations linking him to the case, calling them defamatory, and won interim court relief in April 2026 ordering some posts taken down.
  • The parents say they will continue their protest and have warned of an indefinite hunger strike in Uttarakhand if they are stopped from demonstrating.

The parents of Ankita Bhandari were detained by Delhi Police in the early hours of Thursday during a sit-in at India Gate, as their campaign for a fuller investigation into their daughter's 2022 murder collided with a political dispute over a gubernatorial appointment. Virendra Singh Bhandari and Soni Devi were taken to Tilak Marg Police Station and released in under two hours, according to LawStreet Journal, citing ANI.

What happened at India Gate

Police, accompanied by Central Reserve Police Force personnel, detained the parents at around 3:45 to 4 am, along with Congress MPs including Pawan Khera, Imran Pratapgarhi and Jothimani, according to The Raisina Hills. The detention came a day after Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met the parents at the protest site and backed their demand.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2110379264789057927

After their release, the parents said they would continue their agitation until the appointment was revoked, and warned that if they were prevented from protesting at India Gate they would begin an indefinite hunger strike at their home in Uttarakhand. Congress leaders condemned the pre-dawn detention and accused the government of trying to silence the family.

The appointment at the centre of the protest

The protesters' demand is specific: that the appointment of former BJP national general secretary Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Governor of Sikkim be held until the investigation into the alleged VIP angle is completed. The family and opposition figures allege Gautam is the unidentified VIP referred to during the original investigation — an allegation that resurfaced in late 2025.

Gautam has consistently denied the allegations, describing them as defamatory and politically motivated. He filed a defamation suit, and in April 2026 the Delhi High Court granted him interim relief directing several parties to take down social media posts linking him to the case. That interim order is not a final finding on the truth of the allegations.

The original case

Ankita Bhandari, 19, worked as a receptionist at the Vanantra resort in Uttarakhand's Pauri Garhwal district. She went missing on 18 September 2022 and her body was recovered days later, triggering protests across the state. Resort owner Pulkit Arya and two employees were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment. The family's continuing campaign concerns the separate question of whether an influential guest's alleged demands — raised by a friend during the investigation — were ever fully investigated; the VIP's identity did not feature in the chargesheet against the three convicted men.

What happens next

The family says the agitation will continue, and Congress has said it will stand with them. The legal position, as LawStreet notes, is that a gubernatorial appointment can proceed unless a court finds a disqualifying conviction, so the contest is now political and public as much as legal. Whether the appointment is held, and whether the VIP investigation is formally expanded, are the two developments to watch.
